studies.title: Near transfer to an unrelated N-back task mediates the effect of N-back working memory training on matrix reasoning
studies.authors: Anja Pahor, Aaron R. Seitz & Susanne M. Jaeggi
studies.feature: All modes require updating and retrieval at the exact N-back interval. This work motivates checking progress on unfamiliar updating tasks as well as on the practised game.
studies.positiveFinding: Across three randomized trials involving 460 people, performance on an untrained N-back task statistically mediated transfer to matrix reasoning. The third trial also found an intervention effect on a working-memory composite.
studies.limitation: Two of the three trials did not show an overall intervention effect on matrix reasoning. A mediation result does not mean every participant, or this game, gains intelligence. The publisher's corrected article is linked.

studies.title: Dual n-back working memory training evinces superior transfer effects compared to the method of loci
studies.authors: Wenjuan Li, Qiuzhu Zhang, Hongying Qiao, Donggang Jin, Ronald K. Ngetich, Junjun Zhang, Zhenlan Jin & Ling Li
studies.feature: Relevant to active memory updating and to distinguishing a mnemonic strategy from N-back practice. Spoken and displayed digits offer different presentations of the ordered task here.
studies.positiveFinding: In a study of 148 young adults, dual N-back and method-of-loci groups improved on their trained tasks and digit span. The N-back group also showed faster responses on the highest-load change-detection condition; this was a response-speed result rather than a training-specific accuracy gain.
studies.limitation: The outcomes were memory tasks, not a demonstrated general-intelligence gain. Dual audiovisual N-back differs from ordered digits, and method-of-loci training is not the same as the Da Vinci method.

studies.title: Working memory training revisited: A multi-level meta-analysis of n-back training studies
studies.authors: Anna Soveri, Jan Antfolk, Linda Karlsson, Benny Salo & Matti Laine
studies.feature: Supports N-back as a trainable updating skill and the value of testing an unpractised N-back format. It helps distinguish better game performance from broader transfer.
studies.positiveFinding: A synthesis of 33 randomized controlled studies found a medium-sized benefit on untrained N-back tasks. Smaller benefits appeared on other working-memory measures. The main analysis also found a small positive fluid-intelligence effect (g = 0.16); its significance depended on the analysis, as described below.
studies.limitation: Transfer to fluid intelligence and cognitive control was very small; fluid-intelligence transfer was not significant after the reported control-group adjustment. Most transfer was specific to N-back-like tasks.

studies.title: Improving fluid intelligence with training on working memory: a meta-analysis
studies.authors: Jacky Au, Ellen Sheehan, Nancy Tsai, Greg J. Duncan, Martin Buschkuehl & Susanne M. Jaeggi
studies.feature: Provides a positive research rationale for exploring whether repeated N-back updating can support reasoning beyond the exact trained stimuli.
studies.positiveFinding: Across 20 N-back training studies in healthy adults, the authors found a small, statistically significant average benefit on fluid-intelligence tests.
studies.limitation: This pooled estimate is not a promised IQ increase. Study design and analysis choices matter, and later syntheses such as Soveri et al. found much stronger near transfer than far transfer. No included study tested Ontological Worlds.

studies.title: On the impacts of working memory training on executive functioning
studies.authors: Tiina Salminen, Tilo Strobach & Torsten Schubert
studies.feature: Relates to replacing old information, selecting the correct remembered trial and maintaining task rules despite competing stimuli. The studied task combined auditory letters and visual locations.
studies.positiveFinding: After 14 sessions of dual N-back practice, young adults improved on a separate updating task, aspects of task switching and attentional processing.
studies.limitation: This small study used a passive control group. It found no transfer to its reasoning measure or separate dual-task test. Its auditory and visual streams are not equivalent to the game's multiple ordered digits.

studies.title: Short- and long-term benefits of cognitive training
studies.authors: Susanne M. Jaeggi, Martin Buschkuehl, John Jonides & Priti Shah
studies.feature: Motivates attending to the quality of learning during adaptive practice, rather than assuming that completing sessions alone guarantees transfer.
studies.positiveFinding: In children given game-like working-memory practice, those with substantial training improvement also improved on untrained reasoning tests relative to an active comparison group. The pattern remained at a three-month follow-up.
studies.limitation: The positive result depended on training-gain subgroups rather than a universal benefit. It does not establish the best difficulty threshold, predict a particular user's outcome, or validate this ordered-digit task.

studies.title: Hundred Days of Cognitive Training Enhance Broad Cognitive Abilities in Adulthood: Findings from the COGITO Study
studies.authors: Florian Schmiedek, Martin Lövdén & Ulman Lindenberger
studies.feature: Supports evaluating progress across several different tasks and ability measures. Varied assessment is more informative than a single personal-best game score.
studies.positiveFinding: Younger and older adults completed an extensive programme combining perceptual-speed, working-memory and episodic-memory practice. Positive transfer was found on untrained tests and on broader ability factors.
studies.limitation: The programme involved more than 100 one-hour sessions and many tasks. It cannot show that short N-back sessions, one isolated component, or this particular game produce the same changes.

studies.title: Transfer of learning after updating training mediated by the striatum
studies.authors: Erika Dahlin, Anna Stigsdotter Neely, Anne Larsson, Lars Bäckman & Lars Nyberg
studies.feature: Relevant to the updating operation shared by the modes: keep the relevant information available, replace outdated information and retrieve from the correct temporal position.
studies.positiveFinding: Five weeks of updating practice transferred to an untrained 3-back task. The trained and transfer tasks shared a training-related change in striatal activity.
studies.limitation: Transfer did not extend to a task lacking the shared updating demand, and age-related differences constrained it. Shared brain activity is a mechanism clue, not proof of broad intelligence improvement.

studies.title: Improving fluid intelligence with training on working memory
studies.authors: Susanne M. Jaeggi, Martin Buschkuehl, John Jonides & Walter J. Perrig
studies.feature: An early positive test of adaptive N-back practice using simultaneous auditory letters and visual positions. It motivates the possibility of updating-based transfer while preserving the need to test it independently.
studies.positiveFinding: The authors reported gains on fluid-reasoning measures after dual N-back training, with larger reported gains in groups assigned more training.
studies.limitation: This early finding does not settle the wider mixed literature or establish benefits for ordered digits. The game's spoken sequence and position rule differ from the dual audiovisual task used in the study.
